decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: When is a school bus endorsement needed?
cards.back: A school bus (S) endorsement is needed to carry students between home, school and school-sponsored events in any vehicle built for more than ten passengers.

cards.front: Who can receive a school bus endorsement?
cards.back: Only drivers who are at least twenty-one and already carry either a Class E for-hire license or a commercial license bearing the Passenger (P) endorsement can receive the school bus endorsement.

cards.front: What can happen to a school bus endorsement after a failed drug or alcohol test under school bus law?
cards.back: Failing a drug, alcohol or chemical test given under school bus law can suspend the school bus endorsement for one year.
cards.memory_hook: fail the test, lose a year

cards.front: What must a school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older do to keep it?
cards.back: A school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older must pass school bus skills testing every two years to keep it.

cards.front: What tests are needed to add a motorcycle endorsement?
cards.back: Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle.

cards.front: Which drivers can get endorsements other than school bus and motorcycle?
cards.back: Endorsements beyond school bus and motorcycle are available only to holders of a commercial driver license or commercial learner's permit.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: Where is a renewal reminder mailed, and which permits get none?
cards.back: The Department mails a renewal reminder to the mailing address on your record, but none is sent for a temporary instruction permit or a commercial learner's permit.

cards.front: How can you update the address your renewal reminder goes to?
cards.back: After moving, you can update the address that renewal reminders go to at a local license office or online.

cards.front: How early may you renew, and which tests come with every renewal?
cards.back: You may renew up to six months before the license expires, and every renewal includes the vision and road sign tests.

cards.front: Whose duty is it to renew on time, and what if you drive on a lapsed license?
cards.back: Renewing on time is your own duty even if no reminder arrives, and driving on a lapsed license can earn a ticket for driving without a valid license.

cards.front: What can a license office do if you will be away for a long time?
cards.back: If you will be away from the state or country for a long period, a license office can grant an early renewal.

cards.front: How long can a Missouri license be valid, and may you drive once it expires?
cards.back: A Missouri driver license can be valid for as long as six years, and once it expires you may not drive.

cards.front: When may license and registration renewals be handled in one visit?
cards.back: When the driver license and vehicle registration renewal dates fall within six months of each other, both renewals may be handled in one visit.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: What happens if you renew more than six months after expiration?
cards.back: Missing the renewal by more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days) after expiration means retaking the written and driving tests on top of the vision and road sign tests.

cards.front: How many days does the guide count as six months for a lapsed license?
cards.back: For a license that has lapsed, the guide counts six months as one hundred eighty-four days before the written and driving tests come back.

cards.front: How long do service members have to renew without re-examination after returning?
cards.back: Service members whose license expired while out of state can renew without re-examination for up to six months after an honorable discharge or within ninety days of moving back, whichever comes first, but the expired license still cannot be used to drive.

cards.front: How may armed forces members and dependents renew by mail?
cards.back: Members of the armed forces and their dependents may renew by mail using the Mail-In Driver License Application, Form four thousand three hundred seventeen, with the required documents and fees.

cards.front: How is a lost, stolen or destroyed license replaced?
cards.back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license is replaced with a duplicate, though if it expires within six months you can renew early instead.

cards.front: When can a non-commercial driver renew while suspended or revoked?
cards.back: A non-commercial driver can renew, after the vision and road sign tests, while suspended; during a revocation, renewal is allowed only if the revocation came from refusing a chemical test.

cards.front: When is a renewed license handed back to a suspended driver?
cards.back: A renewed license is not handed back until the reinstatement requirements are met and the driving privilege is restored.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: What does answering yes to the donor question do?
cards.back: Answering yes to the donor question at the counter adds you to the Missouri Organ and Tissue Donor Registry, a first-person consent registry whose decision stands unless you change it and needs no family consent.

cards.front: What does the optional donor symbol look like, and what does it cost?
cards.back: Choosing the optional donor symbol puts a red heart with a green banner on the front of your permit, license or nondriver ID, and neither the symbol nor registry enrollment costs anything.

cards.front: What are you asked after saying yes to the donor registry, and how can you get a sticker?
cards.back: Applicants who say yes to the donor registry are then asked about the optional donor symbol, and a donor sticker for the back of the card can be requested online later.

cards.front: Which donation funds must the clerk ask about?
cards.back: The clerk must ask whether you want to give money to the organ donor fund or the blindness awareness fund.

cards.front: What is the DHH notation, and when must you ask for it?
cards.back: A deaf or hard of hearing applicant may ask for a DHH notation, which must be requested when applying, so emergency and police personnel can quickly recognize the need.

cards.front: Who may add a boater safety indicator, and what does it cost?
cards.back: A Missouri resident holding a current Boating Safety Education Card may add a boater safety indicator, which costs one dollars extra the first time it is added.

cards.front: What does a permanent disability indicator require, and where does it go?
cards.back: A permanent disability indicator goes on the back of the card only with a Physicians Statement (Form five thousand two hundred ninety-four), costs nothing extra and is never required by law.

cards.front: How can a veteran have VETERAN printed on the card?
cards.back: A veteran may have VETERAN printed on the front of the card by showing an accepted discharge document, such as a DD Form two hundred fourteen showing honorable or general under honorable conditions, at no extra cost.

cards.front: What does a medical alert notation require, and where does it appear?
cards.back: A medical alert notation for listed conditions such as diabetes, epilepsy or autism can go on the front of the card with a signed Form five thousand eight hundred thirty-nine, at no extra cost and never by legal requirement.

cards.front: What does the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act require of states?
cards.back: The federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act requires states to close personal information in motor vehicle and license records unless state law directs otherwise.

cards.front: What does the clerk ask about voter registration?
cards.back: At the counter the clerk asks whether you are registered to vote at your current address and can generate updated voter registration for your signature.

cards.front: Who may register with the Selective Service when applying?
cards.back: Male applicants aged eighteen to twenty-six may register with the Selective Service when they apply for a license or permit.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: How can a parent stop a minor from holding a license, and how long does it last?
cards.back: A parent or guardian of an applicant under eighteen can file Form four thousand eight hundred eleven asking the Director of Revenue to deny a license, which also cancels a license already held; the denial lasts until age eighteen or until the parent asks to clear it.

cards.front: Name grounds for losing a license tied to impairment, crashes and applications.
cards.back: A license can be suspended, revoked or denied for driving under the influence, refusing an alcohol or drug test, leaving a crash scene, not filing an accident report, or lying on a license application.

cards.front: Name grounds for losing a license tied to insurance, points, court and support.
cards.back: A license can also be lost for not keeping insurance, too many points, lending your license, skipping court or unpaid tickets, unpaid child support, skipping a required ignition interlock, stealing fuel, a minor possessing liquor, or failing to yield and causing injury or death.

cards.front: Name further grounds involving fake licenses, exam requests, felonies and false insurance proof.
cards.back: Altering your license or using someone else's to buy alcohol, ignoring a Driver License Bureau exam request, using a vehicle in a felony or causing a death in a crash, and submitting false proof of insurance are further grounds for losing a license.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: What does Missouri's GDL law require of first-time drivers under eighteen?
cards.back: Missouri's GDL law makes every first-time driver under eighteen hold an instruction permit and drive with a licensed driver, then drive under restrictions on an intermediate license, before a full license.

cards.front: At what age, with which tests, and for how long is the instruction permit issued?
cards.back: GDL step one, the instruction permit at age fifteen, requires passing the vision, road sign and written tests and is valid up to twelve months depending on document verification.

cards.front: Who must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement?
cards.back: A parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer from a federal residential job training program must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement.

cards.front: Who may ride as the front-seat companion for a permit holder under sixteen?
cards.back: Under sixteen, a permit holder may drive only with a front-seat companion who is a parent, stepparent, grandparent, legal guardian or qualified instructor, or someone at least twenty-five who has been licensed at least three years and has written parent permission.

cards.front: Who may ride as the front-seat companion once a permit holder is sixteen?
cards.back: From age sixteen a permit holder may drive with a front-seat companion who is at least twenty-one and holds a valid license.

cards.front: How does the companion rule change at age sixteen?
cards.back: Under sixteen, a front-seat companion who is not one of the listed relatives, a guardian or a qualified instructor must be at least twenty-five, licensed three years or more and hold written parent permission, while from sixteen any licensed driver aged twenty-one or older qualifies.

cards.front: What must permit drivers and passengers wear, what must be carried, and how is the permit renewed?
cards.back: Permit drivers and all passengers must wear seat belts, the permit itself must be carried because the exam record is not enough, and the permit can be renewed repeatedly without new written tests.

cards.front: How many hours of driving practice are required during the permit period, and who gives them?
cards.back: The permit period must include forty hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, at least ten of them after dark, given by a parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer.

cards.front: What may a physically disabled parent or guardian do about behind-the-wheel instruction?
cards.back: If the parent, stepparent, grandparent or guardian is physically disabled, he or she may name up to two people to give the permit holder behind-the-wheel instruction.

decks.domain: Missouri endorsements, renewal, license loss and the Graduated Driver License steps

cards.front: How long must you hold the permit before the intermediate license?
cards.back: To move to the intermediate license you must hold the permit for at least six months (one hundred eighty-two days), counted from the day after it was issued.

cards.front: How does the guide count the six months for the intermediate step?
cards.back: The intermediate step counts its six months as one hundred eighty-two days, beginning the day after the permit is issued.

cards.front: What record does the intermediate license require?
cards.back: GDL step two, the intermediate license for ages sixteen to eighteen, requires no alcohol-related convictions in the past twelve months and no traffic convictions in the past six months.

cards.front: What must happen at the license office for the intermediate license?
cards.back: An adult from the approved list must come to the license office to confirm the forty hours, and the applicant must pass the driving test and retake the vision, road sign and written tests if earlier results are more than one year old.

cards.front: How many young non-family passengers may an intermediate driver carry in the first six months?
cards.back: In the first six months an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger under nineteen who is not immediate family.

cards.front: How many young non-family passengers may an intermediate driver carry after the first six months?
cards.back: After the first six months the limit becomes no more than three passengers under nineteen who are not immediate family.

cards.front: Which passengers count toward the intermediate passenger limits?
cards.back: Both intermediate passenger limits count only riders younger than nineteen who are outside the driver's immediate family.

cards.front: When may the intermediate passenger limits not apply?
cards.back: The intermediate passenger limits may not apply while the license holder is doing agricultural work.

cards.front: During which hours may an intermediate driver not drive alone, and what are the exceptions?
cards.back: An intermediate driver may not drive alone from one:zero a.m. to five:zero a.m. unless going to or from a school activity, job or emergency, or riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older.

cards.front: Who counts as immediate family for the passenger limits?
cards.back: For the passenger limits, immediate family means parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, and adopted or foster children living in the driver's household.

cards.front: How long is the intermediate license valid?
cards.back: The intermediate license is valid for up to two years, depending on document verification status.

cards.front: What does the full under-twenty-one license require?
cards.back: GDL step three, the full under-twenty-one license at eighteen, requires a valid intermediate license, no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last twelve months, and passing the vision and road sign tests.

cards.front: Over what period are offenses checked for the full under-twenty-one license, and what must not be true when you apply?
cards.back: For the full under-twenty-one license, both alcohol-related offenses and traffic convictions are checked over the last twelve months, and the privilege must not be suspended, revoked or denied when you apply.

cards.front: How long is the full under-twenty-one license valid?
cards.back: The full under-twenty-one license is valid for up to three years, depending on document verification status.

cards.front: What can a new resident transfer, and what does a first-time applicant bring?
cards.back: A new resident can transfer an out-of-state license that is valid or expired no more than one hundred eighty-four days, and a first-time applicant brings the Driver Examination Record (Form one hundred) showing the tests were passed.

cards.front: Where does a driver upgrading a license take the documents for testing?
cards.back: A driver upgrading a license takes the same document set to the Highway Patrol examination site when sitting the written, vision, road sign or driving tests.

cards.front: What does the guide warn about first attempts at the written exam?
cards.back: The guide warns that almost fifty percent of test-takers fail the written exam on the first try, so studying the guide first improves your odds.

recap_hooks.text: A school bus endorsement needs age twenty-one and a Class E for-hire license or a commercial P endorsement.
It can be suspended for a year after a failed test, and holders seventy-five or older retest skills every two years.
A motorcycle endorsement takes written, vision, sign and skills tests, and other endorsements are for commercial holders.
Reminders go to your mailing address, but renewing on time is your duty either way.
Renew up to six months early with vision and sign tests, and ask for early renewal before a long trip.
A license lasts up to six years, and an expired one cannot be used to drive.
Renew more than one hundred eighty-four days late and the written and driving tests come back.
Service members get a window after returning, and military families can renew by mail.
Lost cards get duplicates, and a suspended driver's renewed card is held until reinstatement.
Saying yes joins the donor registry, and the red heart symbol is free and optional.
Notations for hearing, disability, veteran status and medical alerts are optional and mostly free.
Records stay private, and the clerk offers voter and Selective Service registration.
A parent can ask the Director to deny a minor's license until eighteen.
Impaired driving, crashes, false statements, points, unpaid tickets, support and insurance problems can all cost a license.
The GDL permit comes at fifteen after vision, sign and written tests, signed by a parent or guardian in person.
Under sixteen your companion is family, an instructor or a qualifying adult of twenty-five; from sixteen, any licensed driver twenty-one or older.
Everyone buckles up, the permit is carried, and forty practice hours include ten after dark.
Hold the permit one hundred eighty-two days, keep a clean record and pass the driving test for the intermediate license.
Intermediate drivers carry one young non-family passenger at first, three later, and stay off the road alone late at night.
The intermediate license lasts up to two years, and the full under-twenty-one license, after a clean year, up to three.
Transfer a recent out-of-state license, or bring the Driver Examination Record as a first-time applicant.
Almost half of first-time test-takers fail the written exam, so study the guide first.
